newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down, gilt prices little changed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down, gilt prices little changed.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday lower at 3.5-4.0 percent on improved liquidity against opening quotes of 4.75-5.25 percent, dealers said.

"Liquidity with banks is good," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "The February 15 repos auctions drained out only five billion rupees while there was an inflow of 13.8 billion yesterday due to Reserve Bank of India repurchase of securities."
The dealer said call money rates last week had also been affected by adverse sentiment ahead of redemption of India Development Bonds on Friday.
Apprehensions of a tightening in liquidity following redemption of the bonds had led to call money rates crossing the 10 percent mark last week.
"But the redemption did not affect the market in a major way," the dealer added.
Dealers said prices of government securities were steady to firm in brisk trade.
"There was some movement in prices but it was not major," said a dealer.

The zero-coupon 1999 government of India bond traded at 79.28 rupees against its last traded 79.24, the 12 percent 1999 stock at 99.70 against 99.65 and the 12.5 percent 2004 stock at 96.23 rupees compared to its last traded price of 96.27, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturity in April yielded 7.72 percent while July bill yielded 9.35 percent and August bills 9.50 percent, dealers said.
A certificate of deposit maturing in April was traded at a yield of 11.35 percent, they said.
